  REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)  

  Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services  

  RFI Number:  HT941027RFI0001 
 Issuing Activity:  Naval Medical Center San Diego 
 Please submit any questions via email by November 27, 2026  
 Point of Contact:  Dania Suazo, Contract Specialist, dania.suazo.civ@health.mil; Keyshana Harris, Contract Specialist, keyshana.a.harris.civ@health.mil 
 NAICS:  811210 – Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance 
 Estimated Period of Performance:  One 12-month base period with four 12-month option periods, if exercised. 

  1. Purpose  

 This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. The Government is seeking information from capable GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contractors regarding comprehensive repair, maintenance, and lifecycle-support services for a fleet of gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy equipment. 

 This RFI does  not  constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Any future acquisition, if pursued, will be announced separately. 

  2. Background  

 The requiring activity operates a fleet of GI endoscopy equipment used in clinical settings. The fleet currently consists of approximately  58 devices , including flexible endoscopes, ultrasound endoscopes, colonoscopes, gastroscopes, duodenoscopes, enteroscopes, and endoscope reprocessors. A detailed equipment inventory, including manufacturer, model, and serial number where applicable, will be provided as an attachment to this RFI or any future solicitation. 

 The Government is assessing the commercial marketplace’s ability to provide a comprehensive, firm-fixed-price service solution that supports equipment availability, patient-care continuity, maintenance traceability, and lifecycle management. The current equipment list includes Olympus GI equipment and OER-PRO reprocessors. 

  3. Draft Scope of Services  

 The Government seeks industry feedback on the availability and commercial terms for the following services. 

  3.1 Comprehensive Repair and Maintenance  

 The contractor would provide repair and maintenance support for covered equipment, including as applicable: 

 
	 Preventive maintenance consistent with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) recommendations; 
	 Inspection, diagnostics, calibration, functional testing, and quality-control verification; 
	 Component-level repair and replacement; 
	 Repair of insertion tubes, angulation systems, bending rubber, distal tips, imaging components, fiber-optic systems, light guides, connectors, seals, optical components, and mechanical assemblies; 
	 Repair support for endoscope reprocessors; 
	 Documentation of pre-repair condition, work performed, parts repaired or replaced, post-repair testing, and quality-control results; and 
	 Return of equipment in safe functional condition consistent with applicable OEM specifications and regulatory requirements. 
 

 The Government expects a contractor to have qualified technicians, an established quality-management system, and appropriate diagnostic and test equipment to support the identified equipment types. 

  3.2 Service Model and Pricing  

 The Government is interested in commercial service models, including: 

 
	  All-inclusive, firm-fixed-price coverage  for all covered repair, preventive maintenance, calibration, testing, labor, parts, shipping, and administrative support; 
	 A per-device annual pricing structure; 
	 A fixed monthly payment structure; 
	 A hybrid approach combining comprehensive coverage with separately priced services; and/or 
	 Alternative pricing structures that provide predictable costs and transparent exclusions. 
 

 Respondents should identify all coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, repair caps, not-to-exceed limits, surcharges, and conditions that could result in additional Government costs. 

  3.3 Turnaround Time and Service Levels  

 Respondents should address their standard and expedited repair turnaround times, measured from receipt of equipment at the repair facility or initiation of an onsite repair, as applicable. The Government is particularly interested in industry capability to meet the following target ranges: 

  Repair Category  

  Desired Turnaround Time  

 Minor repair 

 1–3 business days 

 Standard repair 

 3–5 business days 

 Major repair/overhaul 

 5–7 business days, subject to parts availability 

 Respondents should also describe: 

 
	 Repair status notifications and tracking capability; 
	 Escalation procedures for delayed repairs; 
	 Performance metrics used to measure on-time completion; 
	 Corrective-action processes for recurring delays or quality issues; and 
	 Emergency or urgent repair support procedures. 
 

 These ranges are based on commercial service levels identified in the available market information and are provided for market-research purposes only.
